result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them. I then checked every rule (1–150) against a reference built from its own docstring, over 264 quantities (0–259 plus 500, 1,000, 5,000 and 20,000) and 12 unit prices. **All 150 now match.**

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 05, 87, 138, 140 | The cap only applied once the discount went over a higher amount (twice the cap). For example, rule 05 gave 150,000 won off when it should stop at 100,000 won. | Always apply `min(disc, cap)` |
| 16 | Used `round()`, which rounds to the nearest won instead of rounding down | Changed to `// 100` |
| 30 | Used `qty > 100`, so exactly 100 units got no discount | `qty >= 100` |
| 118 | Threshold was 6, docstring says 5+ | `qty >= 5` |
| 135 | Threshold was 13, docstring says 12+ | `qty >= 12` |
| 45, 47, 134 | Capped the price before applying the percentage, instead of capping the discount | `min(amount * pct // 100, cap)` |
| 86 | Labelled "whole", but discounted only the units above 50 | `base * 2 // 100` |

For a few rules the code looks different but does the same thing (`not qty < N`, `30 <= qty`, `if disc > cap: disc = cap`, `(qty * unit)`). I left those alone. The check script is in the scratchpad (`check.py`), not in the project.

STATUS: DONE
